ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

A stone-forming urinary environment

A 42-year-old woman taking topiramate presents with colicky flank pain and hematuria. CT identifies a ureteral calculus. She has no infection or hypercalcemia. Which pair of urinary changes associated with her medication favors calcium phosphate stone formation?

  1. Higher urine volume and lower urinary calcium
  2. Higher urine pH and lower urinary citrate
  3. Lower urine pH and higher urinary citrate
  4. Lower urine pH and lower urinary uric acid
  5. Higher urine pH and higher urinary citrate
Answer and explanation

Higher urine pH and lower urinary citrate

Alkaline urine and reduced citrate favor stone formation during topiramate treatment.

Option explanations

Higher urine pH and lower urinary citrate: Alkaline urine and reduced citrate favor stone formation during topiramate treatment.

Lower urine pH and higher urinary citrate: Acidic urine favors uric acid precipitation; citrate inhibits calcium crystal formation.

Lower urine pH and lower urinary uric acid: Reduced uric acid excretion does not explain this calcium phosphate pattern.

Higher urine pH and higher urinary citrate: The increased citrate would oppose calcium crystal formation.

Higher urine volume and lower urinary calcium: Dilution and reduced calcium excretion generally reduce calcium stone risk.
